summary: Senchu Murano was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University and the University of Washington. He served as a professor at Rissho University from around 1957 to 1979.

Specializing in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, Sengaku Mayeda studied at the University of Tokyo and under W. Norman Brown at the University of Pennsylvania. He held posts at Penn, the University of Tokyo, and Musashino University.

A scholar in Buddhist studies, Senkei Sakawa studied at Rissho University, completing his studies by 1965. He was attested as a professor in the Department of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University from 1981 to 1985.

Senmyo Naniwa, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under advisors including Mohan G. Dhadphale. In 2005, he was a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and a professor at Bukkyo University.
Sensho Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was educated at Otani University. He later served as a professor at Otani University from approximately 1991 to 2013.

Sensho Murakami was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Otani University and Toyo University. His career included serving as a professor at the University of Tokyo from 1917 to 1923 and lecturing at Otani University.

Active in religious studies and philosophy, Seraphim Rose studied at USC, under Alan Watts at the California Institute of Integral Studies, and at UC Berkeley. He held a post with the Russian Orthodox Patriarchal Parishes in the United States.

Sergey Oldenburg worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. A student of Ivan Pavlovich Minaev at the University of Saint Petersburg, he served as a professor there, led the Imperial Academy of Sciences, and directed the Asiatic Museum.

Serinity Young was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology who completed her PhD at Columbia University under Alex Wayman. In 2000, she was a research scholar at the American Museum of Natural History and a professor at Southern Methodist University.
Sessō Oda was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under and succeeded Zuigan Goto. His notable students included Sōkō Morinaga and Gary Snyder.

Active in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, Seung-yeon Lee completed doctoral research under Lee Sang-hae. Lee has held posts at the Gyeonggi Institute of Cultural Properties and Sungkyunkwan University.

Seunghak Koh is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Seoul National University and a PhD from UCLA under Robert Buswell. Koh has served as an appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Seungsahn Haengwon, a Buddhist studies and religious figure, studied at Dongguk University and trained under Keum'oh, Keumbong, and Kobong Sunim, whom he succeeded. In 1970, he founded the Kwan Um School of Zen.

Seán McLoughlin is a scholar in religious studies and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Manchester. In 2005, he was attested as a lecturer in South Asian, Islamic, and Religious Studies at the University of Leeds.

Specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology, Shailendra Bhandare has held posts as an assistant keeper at the Ashmolean Museum (attested 2006–2022), a fellow at St Cross College, a curator at the British Museum, and a fellow at the Fitzwilliam Museum.

Shaman Hatley works in Indology and religious studies, completing a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Harunaga Isaacson. He taught at Concordia University and became chair of Asian studies at the University of Massachusetts Boston in 2015.
Shan Shan Zhao is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, also studying with Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.
Shanshan Jia is a scholar of Indology who was attested in 2015 as a doctoral student at the University of Hamburg, studying under Harunaga Isaacson.

Shaoyong Ye is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Peking University under Qing Duan in 2009. He was attested as an associate professor at Peking University from 2010 to 2016.
Sharon J. Roe works in religious studies and philosophy. She pursued doctoral studies at the California Institute of Integral Studies under Steven D. Goodman, attested in 2014.
